events.text: A farm youth nobody has heard of walks into the teahouse with an iron rod and asks which table belongs to the last of the {ranklist}. The whole room points at you. The youth calls themself {challenger_title}.

choices.text: Take the challenge in the street

ok.log: The rod is heavy and honest. Your blade is neither. The youth bows in the dust and asks to be told where they went wrong.

fail.log: The rod finds your ribs on the third exchange. {challenger} takes your place on the list and buys the whole teahouse a round with your loss.

choices.text: Ask the youth who taught them

ok.log: A dead uncle, a single manual, a field to practise in. You talk until dark, and the challenge somehow never happens.

fail.log: The youth will not be talked out of anything. You fight tired, and lose.

events.text: A great sect has let its hidden genius out of five years' seclusion, and the first thing {challenger} does is send a letter: your place, at the sect's foot, in a month.

ok.log: Five years alone taught {challenger} everything except how to fight someone who does not follow the manual. You do not.

fail.log: Five years alone were well spent. {challenger} takes the last place and you take the long road home.

choices.text: Ask for the duel on neutral ground

ok.log: On an open riverbank, away from the sect's cheering disciples, the genius is only a gifted youth. You keep your place.

fail.log: The sect refuses and the murim calls it fear. You lose the place without a blow.

events.text: In a teahouse, {challenger} is already telling a crowd how the last of the {ranklist} will be beaten tomorrow. You are sitting two tables away. Nobody has noticed.

choices.text: Stand up and settle it tonight

ok.log: Tomorrow's story is told tonight, and it ends with {challenger} paying for everyone's tea.

fail.log: {challenger} turns out to be as good as the boast. The crowd has its story, and you are in it the wrong way round.

effects.log: You never fight for a place you have to defend in teahouses. {challenger} takes it unopposed, and finds that a place won without a fight is a thin thing.

events.text: Twins arrive at your door: {challenger} and a sibling who does all the talking. The sibling explains that only one of them will fight you, and will not say which.

ok.log: It was the quiet one. It was also the stronger one. You win anyway, and the sibling stops talking for the first time.

fail.log: It was the quiet one, and the quiet one is very good. {challenger} takes the last place.

choices.text: Watch their feet, and name the fighter

ok.log: You point at the right twin. The sibling laughs, the fighter blushes, and the challenge is withdrawn with a bow.

fail.log: You point at the wrong twin. The right one fights you angry, and wins.

events.text: {challenger}, one place below you on the {ranklist}, arrives with forty friends from a rich family's sect to watch you lose {myrank}.

ok.log: The forty go home quieter than they came. The story of the duel travels faster than they do.

fail.log: The forty cheer. {challenger} takes {myrank} and you get a lesson in fighting before a hostile crowd.

choices.text: Insist on fighting where nobody can watch

ok.log: No crowd, no cheering, no one to fight for but themself. {challenger} loses the nerve and the bout.

fail.log: Alone in the bamboo, {challenger} is still the better fighter today.

events.text: The night before your bout with {challenger}, the inn's tea smells of almonds. Someone on {challenger}'s side, or someone who wants it to look that way.

ok.log: You fight with a heavy head and win with a clear one. {challenger} never knew, and you decide never to tell.

fail.log: You fight half-poisoned and lose {myrank}. Later you learn the poisoner was a gambler with money on the bout.

ok.log: A gambler with money on the bout. You hand him to {challenger}, who is so ashamed that the challenge is withdrawn.

fail.log: You find no one. You fight distracted, and lose.

events.text: {challenger} challenges you, loses the first exchange on purpose, and asks to start again. Then does it again. Something is being studied.

choices.text: Fight the third time for real

ok.log: Let them study. You change your whole style on the third exchange and the notes are worthless.

fail.log: The notes were good. {challenger} takes {myrank} with your own best form turned against you.

choices.text: Stop, and offer to teach instead

effects.log: {challenger} takes the place, and then a lesson a week from you for a year, and becomes the best friend the young murim has seen in a generation.

events.text: On the night of the Lantern Festival, {challenger} challenges you on a boat in the middle of the river, with every lantern in the city watching.

ok.log: One of you goes into the river. It is not you. The whole city sees, by lantern light.

fail.log: You go into the river, lanterns all around, and climb out to applause that is not for you.

choices.text: Fight on the bridge instead, on your terms

ok.log: Solid stone and your footwork. {challenger} never finds a rhythm.

fail.log: Even on the bridge, {challenger} has the better night.

events.text: {challenger}, heir of a great family, sends an invitation embossed in gold: a duel for {myrank} in the family's courtyard, with the patriarch watching and a betrothal hinted at for the winner.

ok.log: You win cleanly. The patriarch watches you leave with an expression that will cause you trouble for years.

fail.log: The heir wins, and the patriarch is relieved. You leave with a bruise and an invitation to dinner you decline.

choices.text: Decline the betrothal in advance, politely

ok.log: The patriarch laughs, the heir relaxes, and the duel becomes a friendly bout in which you keep your place.

fail.log: The patriarch is insulted, the heir furious, and the duel brutal. You lose the place.

events.text: A masked fighter calling themself {challenger_title} challenges you for {myrank}. The mask, the voice and the style are all false. The skill is not.

ok.log: On the last exchange the mask falls. You know the face from your childhood. Neither of you says a word, and you keep your place.

fail.log: The mask stays on. {challenger} takes {myrank} and disappears into the crowd before you can ask.

choices.text: Read the style under the false one

ok.log: You name the true style aloud on the first exchange. The mask bows and withdraws.

fail.log: You guess wrong, and fight the wrong style, and lose.

events.text: {challenger} has been ordered by an elder to take {myrank} from you, and is plainly unhappy about it. The order is in writing.

choices.text: Give {challenger} the fight the elder ordered

ok.log: An honest bout. You win; {challenger} bows, relieved, and the elder has to accept a loss nobody can blame anyone for.

fail.log: An honest bout, and {challenger} wins it. Neither of you looks at the elder.

choices.text: Lose on purpose, and let the elder have the place

effects.log: {challenger} knows exactly what you did. A debt is opened between you that lasts the rest of your lives.

events.text: {challenger} names the place and the hour: the cliff path above the gorge, at the height of the summer storm. Only those who can stand in the wind deserve {myrank}.

ok.log: The wind takes half your stances and all of {challenger}'s. You keep {myrank}, soaked to the bone.

fail.log: The wind favours the one who chose it. {challenger} takes {myrank} with the gorge roaring below.

choices.text: Name a different hour, and wait out the storm

ok.log: {challenger} waits too, and gets cold, and loses the patience the duel needed.

fail.log: The murim calls it fear. {challenger} takes the place without a blow.

events.text: The first place of the {ranklist}. {challenger} challenges you in front of every young name in the murim, gathered for the summer meeting at the Alliance hall.

ok.log: You keep the first place in front of everyone who wanted it. Some of them will be your rivals for life.

fail.log: {challenger} takes the first place in front of everyone. You are second, and the second of a generation is not nothing.

choices.text: Offer a contest of forms instead of blood

ok.log: The hall agrees. Your forms are cleaner. You keep the first place with no one hurt.

fail.log: The hall wants blood. Denied it, they give the place to {challenger}.

events.text: The disciple of the last generation's first Dragon comes for you, carrying the old champion's sword and the old champion's grudge against the list.

choices.text: Fight the sword and the grudge

ok.log: The sword is old and so is the grudge. You keep the first place and the disciple leaves the sword with you, saying it is lighter that way.

fail.log: The old champion's sword is still the best on the list. {challenger} takes the first place.

choices.text: Hand the place over and ask about the old champion

effects.log: {challenger} takes the first place and tells you the story of the old champion, which is worth more than a place.

events.text: A rumour says the Hushed Lantern has been paid to make sure you lose to {challenger}. The duel is at dawn. {challenger} seems to know nothing about it.

choices.text: Fight at dawn and watch the rooftops

ok.log: An arrow comes from a rooftop in the second exchange. {challenger} cuts it out of the air for you, then fights on, and loses honestly.

fail.log: Watching the rooftops costs you the duel. {challenger} takes the first place and learns about the arrow later, with shame.

ok.log: {challenger} postpones the duel and hunts the paymaster with you. The duel, a month later, is clean. You win it.

fail.log: {challenger} thinks it is a trick. You fight distracted at dawn, and lose.

events.text: The challenger for the first place is twelve. {challenger} is the youngest name ever to stand second on the {ranklist}, and is shaking with nerves.

ok.log: You fight properly, which is the only respect a fighter wants. You win. {challenger} cries, and then asks for a rematch next year.

fail.log: You fight properly and the child wins. The youngest first Dragon in history, and you were the one standing there.

choices.text: Give the child the first place

effects.log: {challenger} takes it and knows why, and spends the next ten years earning it. The murim calls you either generous or soft.

events.text: A retired general, {challenger}, has decided after thirty years of war that martial arts are more honest, and wants the last place on the {ranklist} to prove it.

ok.log: The general fights like an army: well, and predictably. You keep your place, and the general keeps your hand a long time afterwards.

fail.log: Thirty years of war is its own kind of method. {challenger} takes the last place and salutes you.

ok.log: By the third pot of tea the general concedes the duel and asks you to lunch next spring.

fail.log: By the third pot of tea the general has learned how you think, and beats you the next morning.

events.text: A merchant prince has hired {challenger} to take a place on the {ranklist}, because his guild wants a ranked master on its letterhead.

ok.log: Hired skill is still skill, but hired nerve is not. {challenger} breaks on the fourth exchange.

fail.log: The merchant got his money's worth. {challenger} takes the place and the letterhead is printed by morning.

ok.log: {challenger} laughs, tears up the merchant's contract, and drinks with you instead.

fail.log: {challenger} is offended, which helps nobody. You lose the place.

events.text: A wandering ascetic from a temple no one can find on a map, {challenger}, asks politely for your place on the {ranklist}. The temple needs the alms a ranked name brings.

ok.log: {challenger} fights with a string of prayer beads you never quite see coming. You keep your place by a hair, and give the temple a donation.

fail.log: The beads find your wrists, then your throat, very gently. {challenger} takes the place and blesses you for it.

choices.text: Give up the place, and the alms besides

effects.log: {challenger} takes the place and your silver, and a temple on no map gets a roof. You are oddly happy all year.

events.text: {challenger} was expelled from your own sect long ago, and has come back with a method nobody in the sect has seen, to take your place on the {ranklist}.

ok.log: The new method is real and so is the old grudge. You keep your place, and send a letter to the sect asking them to reconsider an old expulsion.

fail.log: {challenger} takes your place in front of your own sect's disciples. The elders are very quiet at dinner.

ok.log: An old injustice, an elder long dead. You promise to raise it. {challenger} withdraws the challenge to see if you will.

fail.log: {challenger} does not want to talk about it. The fight happens anyway, and you lose.

events.text: {challenger}'s sect was shamed by you years ago, and {challenger} has climbed the {ranklist} to stand one place below you for exactly this day.

ok.log: Vengeance makes a fighter fast and careless. You keep {myrank}, and suggest the grudge be buried with your blood still in you.

fail.log: Vengeance makes a fighter fast. {challenger} takes {myrank} and the old shame is paid.

choices.text: Apologise for the old shame, publicly

ok.log: Nobody has ever apologised to {challenger}'s sect before. The challenge is withdrawn and the sects trade disciples within a year.

fail.log: The apology is taken as weakness. You lose {myrank} without a blow.

variants: Years ago you shamed {challenger}'s sect. {challenger} has climbed the {ranklist} one rung at a time to stand just below you, for this day.

events.text: {challenger} holds a debt your family owes, and offers to cancel it in exchange for {myrank} on the {ranklist}. Or to fight you for it, debt and all.

ok.log: You keep {myrank} and the debt is cancelled in the same exchange. Your family never learns how.

fail.log: You lose {myrank} and the debt stands. Your family never learns that either.

choices.text: Trade the place for the debt

effects.log: {challenger} takes {myrank} and tears up the debt in front of you. Your family breathes for the first time in years.

events.text: {challenger} has climbed the lists in the same years you did, and now stands one place below you. The challenge comes in a letter that starts, 'I have waited long enough for this fight.'

ok.log: Years of watching each other's names, and the same answer. You both laugh until you cannot stand, and the place is still yours.

fail.log: Years of watching each other's names, and a different answer. {challenger} takes {myrank}, and you buy the wine.

choices.text: Propose fighting for the wine, not the place

ok.log: The place stays where it is and a great deal of wine does not.

fail.log: {challenger} wants the place, not the wine. The fight happens, and you lose it.

variants: {challenger} has risen through the lists alongside you for years and now stands one place below. The challenge arrives by letter: 'I have waited long enough for this fight.'

events.text: {challenger} challenges you for {myrank} and puts a stake on the table: a lost manual, against your own sect's secret method.

ok.log: You win the place and the manual. The lost method fills a gap in your art you did not know was there.

fail.log: You lose the place, and your sect's method goes with {challenger}. The elders will not forgive this one.

choices.text: Fight for the place only, no stakes

ok.log: No stakes, cleaner nerves. You keep {myrank}.

fail.log: No stakes, and still a loss. {challenger} takes {myrank}.

events.text: {challenger} names Mount Tai at dawn for the duel for {myrank}: the oldest stage in the murim, where the masters of every age fought.

ok.log: Dawn on the oldest stage. You keep {myrank}, and the monks of the summit temple write your names in the stone book.

fail.log: Dawn on the oldest stage. {challenger} takes {myrank}, and the stone book has your name in it as the one who lost, which is still a name in the stone book.

choices.text: Ask to fight in your own yard instead

ok.log: {challenger} agrees, curious. In your yard, among your trees, you keep the place.

fail.log: The murim calls it fear of the mountain. {challenger} takes the place.

events.text: {challenger} challenges you for {myrank} and asks only one thing if the challenge is won: that you take one of {challenger}'s disciples into your school.

ok.log: You keep {myrank} and take the disciple anyway. The disciple is the most gifted pupil you will ever have.

fail.log: {challenger} takes {myrank}. You take the disciple, as promised, and are glad of it.

choices.text: Give the place and take the disciple

effects.log: The disciple arrives with one bag and a terrifying talent. {challenger} takes the place and visits often.

events.text: {challenger} has trained under one of the Ten Greatest for twenty years and comes for {myrank} to prove the master's teaching before the master dies.

ok.log: You beat the teaching, which is not the same as beating the master. The master sends a note: 'Good. Come and see me.'

fail.log: The teaching holds. {challenger} takes {myrank}, and an old master somewhere smiles.

ok.log: You sit by the master's bed for a day. {challenger} withdraws the challenge: the master wanted you to meet, not to fight.

fail.log: The master is too ill to see you. The fight comes, and you lose.

events.text: {challenger} and an ally from the masters' list arrive together, asking for {myrank} from you and the place above from the master who stands there. Two duels, one afternoon.

choices.text: Fight yours, and help the other master after

ok.log: You win yours, then stand by the other master, and the pair goes home with nothing. Two masters owe you.

fail.log: You lose yours. {challenger} takes {myrank}. The other master holds, and does not let you forget it.

ok.log: Side by side with the master above you, you break the pair. The list is unchanged and four people have stories.

fail.log: Two-against-two goes badly. {challenger} takes {myrank}.

events.text: The first of the Murim Masters. {challenger} sends challenge cards to every sect in the murim, so that nobody can say they were not told.

choices.text: Answer the cards with a blade

ok.log: The whole murim was told, and the whole murim hears that you are still first.

fail.log: The whole murim was told. {challenger} is first, and you are second in front of everyone.

choices.text: Answer with a card of your own: the day, the place, and no audience

ok.log: A private duel. You are better in private. The murim learns the result and nothing else.

fail.log: The murim calls it fear. {challenger} is first without a blow.

events.text: One of the Ten Greatest has sent {challenger} to fight you for the first place, and to bring back word of whether you are worth inviting up.

ok.log: You keep the first place. The word that goes back to the Ten Greatest is a single sentence, and a good one.

fail.log: {challenger} takes the first place, and the word that goes back is kind, and not enough.

choices.text: Ask {challenger} to tell the Great to come in person

effects.log: {challenger} takes the place and delivers the message. Whether the Great will come is another story.

events.text: {challenger}, the first master of a generation ago, has come out of retirement at eighty, because nobody since has been interesting enough to fight.

ok.log: You are interesting enough. The old master laughs, loses, and goes back into retirement delighted.

fail.log: The old master was right about everyone, including you. {challenger} is first again, at eighty.

choices.text: Ask the old master to teach instead

ok.log: The old master teaches you one form, in one afternoon, and goes home. The place is yours.

fail.log: The old master did not come to teach. The duel happens. You lose.

events.text: A letter with no seal: {challenger} will come for the first place on the night of the new moon, in your own house, while your household sleeps.

ok.log: You hear {challenger} at the third watch, before the door moves. You keep the first place and your household never wakes.

fail.log: {challenger} is past you before you hear a sound. A cut sleeve, a bow, and the first place gone.

choices.text: Lay your house out like a trap

ok.log: {challenger} walks into every trap, laughing, and concedes on the threshold.

fail.log: {challenger} walks around every trap. You lose the first place in your own kitchen.

events.text: A name nobody knew a year ago, {challenger}, has climbed through every list in twelve months and stands at your door for the last place among the {ranklist}.

ok.log: The fastest rise in a generation stops at your gate. {challenger} bows, and promises to be back.

fail.log: The fastest rise in a generation does not stop at your gate. {challenger} is among the Ten Greatest, and you are not.

choices.text: Ask how anyone climbs that fast

ok.log: An inheritance from a ruin in the west, half-understood. You point out the half {challenger} misunderstood. The challenge is withdrawn, gratefully.

fail.log: {challenger} will not say. You fight, and lose.

events.text: A hermit from the snow mountains, {challenger}, has not spoken to anyone in forty years and comes down only to take the last place among the {ranklist}.

ok.log: Forty years of silence, and still a person. You keep your place, and the hermit says one word before leaving: 'Enough.'

fail.log: Forty years of silence is forty years of practice. {challenger} takes the last place without a word.

choices.text: Bow, and let the mountains have the place

effects.log: The hermit takes the place, nods, and goes back up the mountain. The murim does not see {challenger} again for twenty years.

events.text: The Demonic Cult's chosen champion, {challenger}, wants a place among the {ranklist} to prove the Cult is not only an army. The orthodox sects beg you not to lose.

ok.log: You keep the last place. The orthodox sects celebrate. {challenger} does not seem to mind, which worries everyone.

fail.log: {challenger} takes the last place among the Ten Greatest. The orthodox sects will remember who stood there.

choices.text: Ask what the Cult would do with the place

ok.log: A long conversation. {challenger} withdraws, saying you are the first orthodox master worth talking to.

fail.log: {challenger} does not explain anything to the orthodox. The duel happens, and the Cult wins it.

events.text: A master from beyond the western passes, {challenger}, has heard of the Ten Greatest and wants to know if the list is real. Your place is the easiest door.

choices.text: Show the west the list is real

ok.log: The western style is strange and fast and not enough. {challenger} goes home with a story.

fail.log: The western style is strange and fast and exactly enough. {challenger} is among the Ten Greatest, and the murim does not know what to think.

ok.log: A month of exchange. You both leave with something new, and the place stays where it is.

fail.log: {challenger} came to fight, not to trade. You lose the place.

events.text: {challenger}, who stood beside you on the lists since you were both young, has finally caught you on the {ranklist} and comes for {myrank}.

ok.log: A lifetime, one more duel, the same answer. You keep {myrank}, and you both know there will not be another.

fail.log: A lifetime, one more duel, a different answer. {challenger} takes {myrank}, and holds your hand afterwards.

choices.text: Give the old rival the place

effects.log: {challenger} takes {myrank} and knows exactly what you did. It is the only thing you could give that would mean anything.

events.text: The Emperor wants a duel between two of the Ten Greatest for the court's amusement, and has chosen you and {challenger}, the one below you, with {myrank} as the prize.

ok.log: You keep {myrank} before the throne. The Emperor gives you a title neither of you wanted.

fail.log: {challenger} takes {myrank} before the throne. The Emperor applauds; the murim does not.

ok.log: You both refuse. The Emperor is furious and then impressed. The list is unchanged, and the murim is proud of you both.

fail.log: {challenger} does not refuse. You fight before the court, and lose.

events.text: {challenger} has come back from a secret realm in the west changed: the eyes are different, the qi is different. The first thing {challenger} asks for is {myrank}.

ok.log: The inheritance is real but not yet {challenger}'s own. You keep {myrank}, and warn {challenger} about what is living in that power.

fail.log: The inheritance is real. {challenger} takes {myrank} with power that is not entirely human.

choices.text: Find out what the ruin gave

ok.log: You name the inheritance and its price. {challenger} goes pale and returns to the west to give it back.

fail.log: You learn nothing. The fight happens, and the inheritance wins.

events.text: {challenger} is dying, and wants one last duel with someone worthy: you, for {myrank}, so that the end comes as a fighter.

ok.log: You fight the dying master with everything, which is the only kindness either of you wants. You keep {myrank}. {challenger} dies in the spring, content.

fail.log: The dying master fights like the living do not. {challenger} takes {myrank} and gives it back, in a will, to you.

effects.log: {challenger} knows, of course. 'Thank you,' the letter says, after. 'Do not do that again.' It is the last letter that comes.

events.text: {challenger} wants {myrank} before walking through the Last Door: one last proof in this world before leaving it.

ok.log: You keep {myrank}. {challenger} walks through the Gate anyway, laughing, and the sky is quiet for a day.

fail.log: {challenger} takes {myrank} and, a week later, walks through the Gate. The place is empty again, and yours to win back.

choices.text: Ask what is on the other side

ok.log: {challenger} tells you, for an hour, and withdraws the challenge, saying you are closer to the Gate than you think.

fail.log: {challenger} does not know either. The duel happens, and you lose.

events.text: The Martial Alliance asks you, through {challenger}, to step down from {myrank} for the sake of the alliance's balance of power. Or to be removed.

ok.log: The Alliance learns what removal costs. You keep {myrank}, and the Alliance changes the subject.

fail.log: The Alliance's champion removes you. {challenger} takes {myrank}, and the balance of power is restored.

effects.log: {challenger} takes {myrank}. The Alliance owes you, and knows it, and will pay in ways you cannot yet see.

events.text: Your sect and {challenger}'s are at the edge of war. {challenger} proposes that {myrank} decide it instead: one duel, no armies.

ok.log: One duel, no armies. You keep {myrank}, and a war that would have killed hundreds never happens.

fail.log: One duel, no armies. {challenger} takes {myrank}, and the war is avoided anyway, which is what you both wanted.

choices.text: Settle the sects' quarrel at the table

ok.log: The sects settle. The duel is never fought, and the list does not change.

fail.log: The table fails. The duel happens, and {challenger} wins it.

events.text: {challenger} has gone blind in old age and asks for {myrank} anyway, in a dark room, so that you are equal.

ok.log: In the dark you learn how much you rely on your eyes. Not enough to lose. {challenger} laughs and calls it fair.

fail.log: In the dark, {challenger} has a lifetime on you. {myrank} goes to a blind master.

choices.text: Fight in daylight, and tie your own eyes

ok.log: Blindfolded in daylight, you win, and {challenger} insists on buying dinner.

fail.log: Blindfolded, you lose. {challenger} takes {myrank} and gives you the blindfold to keep.

events.text: First Under Heaven. {challenger}, second on the list, comes to your mountain for the oldest duel in the murim: the first place, the first light, no witnesses but the sky.

ok.log: The sun comes up on two masters and one first place. Still yours.

fail.log: The sun comes up and {challenger} is First Under Heaven. You walk down the mountain lighter than you have been in years.

choices.text: Step aside for the next age

effects.log: You give the first place to {challenger} at the top of the mountain, and walk down a legend rather than a champion.

events.text: Three of the Ten Greatest, led by {challenger}, propose that First Under Heaven should be decided again, among all of you, by a contest no one has held in a century.

choices.text: Defend the first place in the contest

ok.log: A week of duels. On the seventh day the first place is still yours, and nobody will ask again for a generation.

fail.log: On the seventh day {challenger} is First Under Heaven. The murim will talk about the contest for a hundred years.

choices.text: Convince them the contest is beneath them

ok.log: They agree, sheepishly. The first place stays with you, and the murim never learns how close it came.

fail.log: They do not agree. The contest happens without your heart in it, and {challenger} wins.

events.text: {challenger}, second on the list, has studied every duel you ever fought, and comes for First Under Heaven the way you would: without mercy and without asking twice.

choices.text: Fight the student you never taught

ok.log: You win, barely, and you have never been prouder of anyone you beat.

fail.log: {challenger} is First Under Heaven. Everything of yours, used well. You walk home happy.

choices.text: Hand the first place to the one who learned from you

effects.log: You hand it over with a bow. {challenger} weeps, takes it, and keeps it for a generation.

events.text: Heaven itself seems to send {challenger}: a master no one knew existed, who arrived with a thunderstorm and asks for First Under Heaven as if it were owed.

ok.log: Thunder all through the duel, and then silence. You are still First Under Heaven, and the sky clears as if embarrassed.

fail.log: {challenger} takes First Under Heaven with lightning in the eyes. Heaven, it seems, had its favourite.

ok.log: {challenger} does not know. Neither do you. The duel is set aside while you both find out.

fail.log: {challenger} does not answer questions. You lose the first place in the storm.
